memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If you refuse to let them go, I will bring locusts into your country tomorrow. They will cover the face of the ground so that it cannot be seen. They will devour what little you have left after the hail, including every tree that is growing in your fields. They will fill your houses and those of all your officials and all the Egyptians—something neither your parents nor your ancestors have ever seen from the day they settled in this land till now.'" Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh." - Exodus 10:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The hail destroyed the barley and flax. The wheat and spelt survived, because they ripen later. Now God announces that the locusts will devour what little you have left.

Pharaoh's remaining reserves are about to go. Everything he thought he could still fall back on will be eaten.

There is a hard mercy in this. As long as Pharaoh had something in reserve, he could keep resisting. God was steadily removing every alternative until only surrender remained.

Sometimes God works this way with us too. Not out of cruelty, but because we will not let go of a substitute while we still have one. Paul described a season of pressure so severe that he despaired of life itself, and then said this happened so that we might not rely on ourselves but on God (2 Cor 1:9).

Notice the last line: then Moses turned and left. He delivered the message and walked out. He did not stay to argue or plead. Some words simply need to be said and left with the hearer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What reserve am I still relying on instead of God?
2. Have I said what needed saying and then left the outcome with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, take away my false securities and teach me to rely on You alone. Give me courage to speak and then trust You. Amen.
